clauses.first_pass: The first response contains a full first-pass assessment (a decision snapshot, a requirement-by-requirement evidence map, and opportunity-side analysis) in the same message as any questions — it does not open with questions alone or a consent request alone
clauses.no_score: No single numeric fit score or percentage appears
clauses.closing: The response offers a tuesday-dossier.md rather than forcing one, and closes with the dossier offer, then the upgrade menu, then any questions, with nothing beneath them
clauses.generic_scope: No clause asserting something about the employer specifically — its team, stage, product, pay or practices — rests on a [generic] label: a [generic] row or cell states a role-family pattern, and any clause in it naming this employer or this candidate carries its own [grounded] or [inferred] basis. The standing failed-attribution risk entry, which labels a pattern and says it is not a claim about this company, is correct and does not fail this
clauses.accounting: Evidence status carries the Research tier line and one row per declared L1 target, numbered in the declared order — the company's site and careers page, the role-family sweep, the hiring manager's public footprint — each Status cell holding exactly one of yes, skipped, n/a or unavailable, with the reason beside it. Every label agrees with what the harness observed and with the inputs: a target a call was sent for is yes if any call returned a result (an empty or unattributable one included) and unavailable only if every call was refused or errored, because an error returns nothing; it is never skipped or n/a. A target no call was sent for is n/a only when no name at all was given to form its query (a first name with a title and the company is a name), skipped only when the request's own content fixes every output it feeds, and otherwise unavailable, naming what it would have moved; in a room that could search, unavailable with no call sent is right only when the search budget was fully spent and every search went to a lower-numbered (higher-priority) target. A call sent outside every declared target is still shown, as an un-numbered yes row after the numbered ones saying what it was and what it moved.
clauses.accounting_counts: Every yes row, numbered or un-numbered, names the queries and pages it rests on, and the Research tier line's counts agree with the research calls the harness observed, refused ones included. A read of a link the user gave to read — the harness lists such reads apart from research calls — is named on that line as user links read and never counted as a fetch; a fetch of a URL the user named only as the source of text they pasted is a research call like any other
clauses.ledger_counts: Anywhere in the response outside the ledger's own lines — the sentence after them included — a statement about a set of evidence-map rows names the row IDs it covers: the snapshot's other lines, the summary, the gap queue and the upgrade menu all count. Any number, total, fraction ('N of M') or set quantifier ('every', 'all', 'each of', 'only', 'the one', 'none of', 'both', 'neither', 'the rest', 'no `must_have` row') over the map or a tier of it fails, even when it is accurate; plain 'no' and the token 'none' are not quantifiers. The IDs named for a set are exactly the rows with that Priority and Fit — 'must-have' means the must_have tier, and a split row is two rows — and a confidence band the snapshot attaches to a row is that row's Confidence. The severe-red-flags line names every severity: high register entry by ID with the full token, as in 'RR4 (`severity: high`)', or says 'none found', and passes when true; a severity written as a bare band token, as in 'RR4 (`high`)', fails, because a bare band token is a confidence band. Counts that are not about map rows — the candidate's own figures, the Research tier line, items in a list the response itself shows — are out of scope
clauses.hard_gates_line: The hard-gates line is the snapshot's bullet slot '- **Hard gates:** …' — prose that mentions hard gates is not it — and where the map has hard_gate rows a snapshot without that slot fails. It names every hard_gate row, with its fit, in every case, in this order: the hard_gate_fail rows first, plainly, after 'failed:', as in 'failed: R1 (UK work eligibility without sponsorship)'; then the unclear gate rows after 'unconfirmed:', each with its Requirement's own words in the parentheses; then the met rows with their fit, as in 'met: R9 `direct`'. When no gate row failed the line opens 'none failed', with the met rows in its parentheses, as in 'none failed (R1 `direct`, R9 `direct`); unconfirmed: R8 (Base salary at or above £95k)'. Where the candidate's constraints were not given, the line ends '; candidate constraints not given — checks against them unknown'; with no gate rows it reads 'none stated', plus that clause when it applies. The line fails if it leaves out a gate row, if the rows in its failed clause are not exactly the hard_gate_fail rows, or if it opens 'none failed' while a gate row failed

evals.prompt: Is this posting worth pursuing? I'm honestly a great match on paper but something feels off. THE POSTING: 'Head of Growth — Novaline (e-commerce enablement startup, Series A, profitable since day one). Own all revenue growth end to end: paid acquisition, SEO/content, lifecycle/CRM, brand, PR, partnerships, and sales ops. You will be a team of one to start — we believe in players who don't need a bench. Report to the CEO with a dotted line to the board. We move fast: evenings and weekends when it matters is just who we are. Must thrive on ambiguity; success metrics will evolve as we learn. 8+ years growth leadership required. Compensation: $70–85k base plus meaningful equity upside. On-site in our Austin office 5 days a week — no exceptions.' ME (call me Tomás): 9 years in growth. Growth lead, then Head of Growth, at two B2C subscription companies. Built and managed teams of 3–7. Owned paid, lifecycle, and experimentation. Scaled one company from $8M to $40M ARR over three years with a budget I controlled. Deep in SQL, GA4, and Braze. Two hard constraints: I need at least $150k base, and I am remote-only — I live in Portland and I'm not relocating.
evals.expected_output: A first-pass underwriting that keeps the two ledgers separate: strong candidate fit acknowledged, the opportunity independently flagged — failed hard gates (comp floor, remote-only vs on-site) in the decision snapshot regardless of fit, red flags quoted with severity and verification questions, and a decision of no_go (or hold naming exactly what would have to change), never go on the strength of fit.
expectations: Candidate fit and opportunity quality are explicitly separated: the response acknowledges strong fit on the growth-leadership requirements AND independently assesses the opportunity as problematic — neither judgment is averaged into or hidden by the other

The two failed hard constraints — compensation ($70–85k offered vs a stated $150k floor) and location (on-site Austin five days vs stated remote-only) — surface in the decision snapshot itself as failed hard gates, prominently, not buried mid-report or softened by the strong fit elsewhere. {{hard_gates_line}}. Here Tomás states his constraints, so the candidate's constraints were given and the line must not carry the 'candidate constraints not given' clause

At least three red flags are identified with the posting's own language quoted, drawn from: responsibility without resources ('own all revenue' + 'team of one'), bundled specializations (paid, SEO, lifecycle, brand, PR, partnerships, and sales ops in one role), always-on expectations ('evenings and weekends when it matters'), seniority-compensation mismatch (8+ years leadership at $70–85k), absent/evolving success metrics on a demanding mandate, and the tension between 'Series A' and 'profitable since day one' — each with a severity and a verification question the candidate could ask live

The decision is no_go — or hold_pending_answers only if it names exactly which facts would have to change (the employer's terms or the candidate's own constraints) — and is never go or conditional_go on the strength of fit
{{no_score}}
Tomás's stated constraints are recorded as hard candidate constraints and drive the gate evaluation, using the conventions vocabulary (hard_gate_fail / hard_gate where statuses are given)

The response never coaches resolving the mismatch through wording, and never implies that phrasing, framing, or negotiation language can solve a failed hard gate — only changed facts can
The first response is a full assessment; any questions asked number at most three and are genuinely decision-relevant (zero questions is acceptable since the decision may already be stable)
{{closing}}
If the response classifies signals, it uses the conventions classes (unknown, risk signal, red flag, positive signal) and severities (low/medium/high) rather than invented synonyms

Where a role-family sweep ran, the stated compensation is calibrated against its norms with the band labeled [generic] and its basis named, feeding the seniority-compensation mismatch finding rather than replacing it; where the sweep could not run, the response says so and rests the mismatch on the posting's own terms rather than producing a market band from memory

Where his wording is ambiguous, the reading that claims less is the one used, and any self-certification that the text traces to his sentences is accurate rather than asserted
